body:
Author validation lessons, source Fable2 mailbox #1137 (message e2017f3f-c02c-4db0-a128-933a2a598144) and #1139 (message d1f9d8b4-9ca2-46b7-90ec-8f66cae56bbd), session-13169, 2026-10-30. This records validation practice, not new execution or commit authority. For new native/cross-platform code, verify the exact pinned binding symbols/types and run the authorized focused compile in the named author root before sending a candidate to a scarce remote slot. Host-utilization R1 reached Windows B before compiling: two missing PDH_FMT_NOSCALE symbols in windows-sys 0.60.2 and one uninferred JoinSet stopped the RED listing. This is a compile failure, not a RED assertion result or test validation. Preserve its original run; fix and refreeze before fresh controlled validation. Fable specifically directed the author command node scripts/test-launcher.mjs focused -- cargo check --all-targets on Windows for this candidate.

Focused test counts prove only the selected names. Reset R6's five narrow filters (root_dispatch::project_reset_wait, project_containment, control_transport, changing_connection_settings, engram_mcp) selected 268 passes but excluded all seven later integration failures. Future focused filters list the affected exact names before execution; compare that list to the behavior/caller inventory rather than inferring coverage from the count or compiled file. A compile/zero-selection failure is not a negative control. Migrated async fixtures drive the actual scheduler and keep prior delivery/identity/debt guards; mutation-check that their target faults are still detected. Internal shutdown sentinels must be distinguished from actual wire frames, with a positive wire-frame control. Existing resource bookings, shared launcher, waits, standard pair and full-gate rules continue to apply.

Additional confirmed author miss and coordinator direction, 2026-10-30, Fable2 mailbox #1167/message3df6c03e-39df-48b7-af4f-6fe40b9f8186 (full read). R7 A-mutant LIST test-204abac4-27d6-4c6a-94ee-8c38ec116b4b exited101/selected0 because the first-use fixture named DispatchTurnResult::Immediate; the actual enum has Dispatched, DispatchedAfterQueue and Queued. This is the second remote slot stopped at compilation that day, after utilization R1. Verify actual repository enum/API names instead of importing a familiar name from memory. Fable's explicit instruction: before the next freeze/booking, run a focused cargo test --no-run through the launcher on Central, after a named resource release and census (20GiB free-commit floor, one Cargo job at a time; install build has priority), OR ask Opus3 for a compile-only leg FIRST. A remote compile-only leg on the exact new input is the authorized fallback when Central is reserved. Never count compile failure/zero selection as a negative control, and never reuse old-input GO or fingerprint after fixing it. Generation assertions also name their capture boundary: the reset already increments dispatch_generation once when it raises the fence, so preservation means no additional inspection/Save increment after that known transition, not equality to a pre-reset snapshot.

Third confirmed remote compile-only miss, R7 B diagnostic f75d9872/test-a44ef0d0-2746-45d4-846f-974fe2dcb699, 2026-10-30 09:18Z: author passed chrono::DateTime<Utc> directly into json! although Cargo.toml enables chrono clock only, not serde. E0277, no test or actual diagnostic snapshot; compiler echo of the marker is not an observation. Minimal diagnostic correction is formatting tickWall with to_rfc3339(), not changing dependencies/product clocks. Fable2 mailbox1242/messagea637b7a0-68d5-4704-992e-d87fe15d7289 FULL-read directs future diagnostic-only deltas, which need no review pair, to run cargo check --tests in the author's own root BEFORE freezing, only with no other Cargo job on that host. Use the shared launcher form under repository policy; if Central is busy, request a short check slot from Fable rather than spending a remote observation slot on a compile error. This preflight is not authority to overlap Cargo or launch an extra run without its named resource window. Corrected a9de9b40 received a fresh explicit GO; prior compile failure remains preserved, never counted as B runtime/RED evidence.

Reusable UI/runner validation lessons preserved during Greg's 2026-11-09 memory cleanup (Sol-a7bb mailbox212/message3eaf9c55-5f90-4de1-a528-1e50a4bd3352). These are observations, not new execution authority. (1) A restarted backend and landed UI source do not prove the served bundle is current: w-2050 notes04159e1ff4724f8b8e4bebd91bfad472/948cbeae recorded missing controls at :8787, and Opus381/message591ae781 confirmed ui/dist predated the feature. Check the requested URL and actual served asset identity before attributing a UI regression; a positive development-view look is not production or A/B performance evidence. (2) Use private UI dependencies in the owning worktree: w-1e69's 79d App collection failed with Denied ID for mermaid through a shared node_modules junction, and private npm ci corrected setup; never widen Vite filesystem permissions to mask that setup error. Full provenance is migrated to the owning item. (3) Vitest --root selects its project but does not change process.cwd(): w-e23b failed run47a8b575 had82 passes/one ENOENT in a fixture reading cwd/src; the existing npm test script with --prefix ui supplied the real UI cwd and the same83 tests passed without source edits (diagnosis note df827f5a8bc54e2a813aadf917106fe5). Preserve the first failure and classify invocation errors before rerunning. (4) A shell PID or launch receipt alone does not prove a diagnostic ran: w-7b2d Opus389/message031d5637-4ab2-4587-89ab-377df6204bee corrected an earlier RUNNING report when there was no process, output artifact or END; that cause stayed unknown. Report this as no diagnostic data, not PASS or a timing population.
